title: Yaakov of Kefar Sikhnya

paragraphs: Yaakov of Kefar Sikhnya, one of that man’s disciples. [Avodah Zarah 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.17a.1-2) relates that Rabbi Eliezer told Rabbi Akiva how Yaakov once asked him: “Your Torah says, ‘You shall not bring a harlot’s hire,’ etc. May it be used to make a privy for the High Priest?” Rabbi Eliezer says that he answered nothing. Yaakov told him: “Thus I was taught: From filth they came; to filth they shall go.” The explanation pleased Rabbi Eliezer, and because of this he was punished. [Kohelet Rabbah 1:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.1.8.3) also has the account. Perhaps he is Yaakov of Kefar Samma in [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 14:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.14.4.12), who sought to heal Rabbi Elazar ben Dama in that man’s name, but Rabbi Yishmael prevented him. The end of [Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.2.2.11) also has this.[^1]
[Kohelet Rabbah 7:26](https://www.sefaria.org/Kohelet_Rabbah.7.26.3) calls him Yaakov of Kefar Sessma.[^2]

notes.text: Rabbi Eliezer is the speaker in the marketplace account. Elazar ben Dama is the person Yaakov tries to heal in the other episode. The [Bavli’s healing parallel](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.27b.6-9) calls the village Sikhnya, as does Kohelet Rabbah 1:8.
Both linked Jerusalem Talmud passages give Kefar Samma. Kohelet Rabbah 7:26 has Sama, where Hyman writes Sessma. Hyman leaves the identification tentative.
